screening_notes: Deep learning is used (ResNet), CT modality, quantitative metrics reported, and lungs (an organ) are segmented. The paper also focuses on COVID-19 lesions, but lung segmentation is included, so organ segmentation is partially met. The primary exclusion is the 2D processing.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (3D CNN), 3D volumetric processing, organ segmentation (cardiac structures), CT modality, quantitative metrics (DSC, ASSD), and novel contribution (training on virtual non-contrast images from dual-energy CT to segment non-contrast CT).
title: Deep Learning from Dual-Energy Information for Whole-Heart Segmentation in Dual-Energy and Single-Energy Non-Contrast-Enhanced Cardiac CT

postprocessing: Connected component labeling; keep largest component for each structure except pulmonary artery trunk (multiple components allowed)
datasets: ["Dual-energy set (18 patients, CLARITY study)", "Single-energy set (218 routine clinical care + 72 orCaScore study, total 290)"]

screening_notes: The paper describes integration of a deep learning-based prostate organ and lesion segmentation pipeline into a clinical PACS environment using multiparametric MRI. It does not use CT scans, so it does not meet the CT modality requirement.
exclusion_reason: Modality is MRI (mpMRI), not CT. The paper focuses on prostate MRI segmentation and clinical deployment, failing the CT modality inclusion criterion.
title: Research-based clinical deployment of artificial intelligence algorithm for prostate MRI

screening_notes: Uses deep learning for spleen segmentation, reports Dice 0.96, but no novel architecture or methodological improvement; it's an application of existing U-Net.
exclusion_reason: Only applies existing methods (U-Net via MIScnn) without methodological contribution; the paper's focus is on clinical prognostic application, not on novel segmentation architecture or significant improvement.
title: Fully automated AI-based splenic segmentation for predicting survival and estimating the risk of hepatic decompensation in TACE patients with HCC

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (nnU-Net), 3D volumetric processing, organ segmentation (lungs), CT modality, quantitative metrics (DSC, NSD), novel contribution (CTPA-specific model with external validation).
title: External validation, radiological evaluation, and development of deep learning automatic lung segmentation in contrast-enhanced chest CT
architecture_details: Two-stage cascade 3D nnU-Net
loss_function: Not explicitly stated; nnU-Net typically uses combined Dice and cross-entropy loss
preprocessing: Truncating HU range to -1024 to 2500, then normalisation using SD (199 HU) and mean (-761 HU) of segmented lung region across all training images. Resampling to mean pixel size of 1.01x1.01x0.84 mm for first stage and 0.75x0.75x0.625 mm for second stage. Data augmentation: random rotation (-30° to 30° about 3 axes, p=0.2), scaling (0.7 to 1.4, p=0.2), gamma correction (0.7 to 1.5, p=0.3), mirroring about 3 axes (p=1).
postprocessing: Removal of regions < 250 ml in volume.
dataset_size: Training: 29, validation: 8, test: 12, radiological evaluation: 176 (internal); external: 28. Total 225 PH and 28 ILD patients.
comparison_methods: ["Not directly compared; referenced published methods (e.g., Yoo et al., Hofmanninger et al.)"]
limitations: Training set contains only patients with known PH, thin-slice volumetric CTPA protocol scans, from a single tertiary centre with predominantly white European population. Lack of truly 'normal' scans. Lack of rare cases. Intended clinical use limited to patients with suspected PH.
future_work: Develop and test the DL model in a large cohort of multiethnicity patients. Transfer learning to improve performance for both contrast and non-contrast imaging.

screening_notes: Paper uses deep learning (nnU-Net) as primary method, processes 3D CT volumes, segments kidney (organ) and renal tumor, reports quantitative metrics (Dice, Jaccard, MSD), and presents a novel exponential-plateau method for determining dataset size requirements. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Effect of Dataset Size and Medical Image Modality on Convolutional Neural Network Model Performance for Automated Segmentation: A CT and MR Renal Tumor Imaging Study

preprocessing: nnU-Net automatic preprocessing; CT images cropped around kidneys and resampled to 256x128; MR T2-weighted images used; resampling and normalization as per nnU-Net
postprocessing: Majority voting ensemble of five sub-models

screening_notes: The paper explicitly states that FC_DenseNet is a two-dimensional model, processing CT slices independently. It does not use 3D convolutions or volumetric context, failing criterion 2 for 3D/volumetric processing.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context
title: Automatic delineation of organs at risk in non-small cell lung cancer radiotherapy based on deep learning networks
architecture_details: DenseNet-based fully convolutional network with dense blocks, transition down/up modules, bottleneck architecture (1x1 convolution), and skip connections
loss_function: Cross-entropy loss
preprocessing: Grey value mapping to 0-255, window width 400, level 40, data cleaning and augmentation
postprocessing: Early stopping; selected epoch 30; no explicit postprocessing

limitations: Two-dimensional model lacks spatial continuity; small training dataset; heart and cord segmentation challenging due to class imbalance and weak features
future_work: Suggests exploring 3D models for better spatial feature extraction; discusses three development directions including deeper/wider networks and 3D U-Net variants

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning primary, 3D CT volumes, organ segmentation, CT modality, quantitative metrics, novel contribution (ensemble segmentation+registration).
title: Comprehensive 3D Analysis of the Renal System and Stones: Segmenting and Registering Non-Contrast and Contrast Computed Tomography Images
architecture_details: Ensemble of segmentation models (3D U-Net, ResU-Net, Swin UNETR) with rigid registration for multi-phase CT fusion
loss_function: Dice loss (nnU-Net default) for segmentation; Mutual Information (MI) and Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC) for registration
preprocessing: Intensity clipping to 0.5-99.5 percentile, Z-score normalization, resampling to target spacing (2.5, 0.754, 0.754 mm), data augmentation (nnU-Net default)
postprocessing: Rigid registration of segmentation results from different phases using ITK library, label fusion with priority order (artery > stone > collecting system > medulla > parenchyma)
datasets: ["In-house dataset from First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University (three-phase CT: NCT, CTC, CTE)"]
dataset_size: 464 patients, 1392 CT scans (three phases per patient)
other_metrics: {"Hausdorff Distance": "Reported per organ and method (e.g., kidney HD 17.76 mm for Swin UNETR)", "Registration metrics": "Dice and HD for registration evaluation (e.g., best registration Dice 93.28% with ResU-Net, Separate+MI)"}
comparison_methods: ["3D U-Net", "ResU-Net", "Swin UNETR", "Registration methods: baseline (segmented outcomes, separate), extended methods (whole, entire CT, etc.)"]
limitations: Slow speed due to time-consuming registration process (44.5s per sample)
future_work: Replace conventional registration with deep learning-based approach to reduce time; expand dataset and conduct clinical validations

screening_notes: Deep learning primary method (InceptionResNetV2 + UNet3+), processes 3D CT volumes via multi-planar 2D networks combined into 3D, segments cardiac organs, uses CT, reports Dice and Hausdorff metrics, and presents a novel cascaded pipeline.
title: Automatic Cardiac Structure Contouring for Small Datasets with Cascaded Deep Learning Models
authors: L. B. van den Oever et al.
architecture_details: Two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 uses InceptionResNetV2 to classify axial slices containing heart; Stage 2 uses three UNet3+ networks on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices, combined by multiplication of binary masks.
loss_function: Segmentation: hybrid loss = 2 * focal loss + dice loss; Classification: binary cross entropy
preprocessing: CT images converted to NUMPY, contrast adjusted to mediastinum window (W:350 HU, L:50 HU); no other preprocessing
postprocessing: Combination of three networks' outputs by multiplication of binary masks
datasets: ["Internal planning CT dataset (UMCG breast cancer patients)"]
dataset_size: 50 CT scans total; 41 training, 3 tuning, 6 validation for segmentation stage
other_metrics: {"95% Hausdorff distance (mm)": {"whole heart": 1.86, "right ventricle": 2.98, "left ventricle": 2.02, "left atrium": 6.46, "right atrium": 6.16}, "volume ratio": {"whole heart": 0.96, "right ventricle": 0.99, "left ventricle": 1.05, "left atrium": 0.8, "right atrium": 0.84}}
comparison_methods: ["Choi et al. (DL)", "Harms et al. (DL)", "Jung et al. (atlas)", "Luo et al. (atlas)"]
limitations: Struggles with caudal and cranial parts of heart; difficulty near apex; underperforms for atria; non-contrast scans with thick slices and cardiac motion; ground truth variability.
future_work: Qualitative evaluations; training on contrast scans; possibly combining contrast and non-contrast scans.

screening_notes: Paper uses deep learning (2D and 3D U-Net) for segmentation of the prostatic urethra on planning CT images. It processes 3D volumes (3D U-Net) and reports quantitative metrics (centerline distance, PWR). Novel contribution: new method for prostatic urethra segmentation with large dataset. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Development of deep learning-based novel auto-segmentation for the prostatic urethra on planning CT images for prostate cancer radiotherapy
architecture_details: 2D U-Net: 3 residual units, channels 16,32,64,128,256; 3D U-Net: 4 residual units, channels 32,64,128,256,512. Implemented with MONAI.
loss_function: Dice Cross Entropy Loss (DiceCELoss)
preprocessing: Input data created from bladder and prostate contours (not CT images). DICOM RT Structure Set converted to binary images, resampled to 1mm voxel size, brightness values set (bladder=64, prostate=128). Output urethra=255. For 2D, projected 3D data in coronal and sagittal directions. Cropped to 128x128x128 (3D) or 256x256 (2D).
postprocessing: Predicted coordinates used to draw a circle of diameter 5mm on each CT slice, then resampled to original pixel size.
datasets: ["Tohoku University Hospital dataset (430 patients with localized prostate cancer)"]
dataset_size: 430 patients (70% training, 10% validation, 20% test)
comparison_methods: ["2D U-Net vs 3D U-Net", "Cubero et al. (deep learning on CT for brachytherapy)", "Belue et al. (deep learning on MRI)", "Takagi et al. (multi-atlas method)"]
training_time: Approximately 6 hours for 2D models, 24 hours for 3D model
limitations: Ground truth from urethral catheter may include deformation errors; cases with asymmetrical urethra due to prostate hypertrophy have reduced accuracy; some cases may have significant errors hindering clinical use.
future_work: Incorporate factors like benign prostatic hyperplasia; increase number of irregular cases; use MRI images to resolve catheter deformation.

screening_notes: The paper presents a hybrid method combining DL, atlas-based registration, and geometric models. DL is used only for the whole heart, not for the 17 other substructures. Although quantitative metrics are reported and CT is used, the primary segmentation method is not deep learning.
exclusion_reason: Deep learning is not the primary segmentation method. The proposed approach is a hybrid that uses deep learning (nnU-Net) only for whole heart segmentation, while the majority of cardiac substructures are segmented via multi-atlas mapping and geometric modeling. Thus, it does not meet the criterion of deep learning as the primary method.
title: Open-source, fully-automated hybrid cardiac substructure segmentation: development and optimisation

screening_notes: The proposed method uses a 2D SegNet architecture applied slice-by-slice to CT volumes, without 3D convolutions or volumetric context. It fails the 3D/volumetric processing criterion.
exclusion_reason: Only processes 2D slices without 3D context
title: Automatic Liver Segmentation from Multiphase CT Using Modified SegNet and ASPP Module
architecture_details: Modified SegNet with four encoder-decoder pairs, ASPP module (dilation rates 6, 12, 18), leaky ReLU activation, VGG-16 encoder initialization
loss_function: Cross entropy
preprocessing: Convert to Hounsfield units, convert to unsigned 8-bit, crop background, resize to 384x384x3, augmentation (scaling and translation)
dataset_size: Training: 4994 CT images from 3D-IRCADb, LiTS, KMC; Test: 10 CT volumes (KMC) and 20 CT volumes (CHAOS)
gpu_used: NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB memory
limitations: The model has not identified the IVC in many cases. Another shortcoming is its sensitivity to the CT image format. Although it was trained using CT images in DICOM and NIFTI formats, the algorithm works better on the former and gives inferior results for CT images in the latter format.
future_work: Constructing a hepatic CADx system for differentiating between normal and abnormal liver and diagnosing liver cancer.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning primary, 3D processing, organ segmentation, CT, quantitative metrics, novel contribution.
title: Deep learning-based whole-heart segmentation in 4D contrast-enhanced cardiac CT
architecture_details: Encoding path with two downsampling layers with strided convolutions, six residual ResNet blocks, decoding path with two upsampling layers with transposed convolutions, 3D batch normalization, softmax output.
loss_function: Negative sum of soft Dice similarity coefficients
preprocessing: Resampled to 0.8x0.8x0.8 mm3 isotropic resolution, CT numbers linearly rescaled to [0,1] range. No data augmentation.
postprocessing: During testing, 3D CNN output probability maps were combined across image patches by averaging, and the largest connected component of each structure was retained in the final segmentation mask.
datasets: ["Internal clinical dataset (TAVI patients)", "Multi-modality whole heart segmentation challenge (MMWHS)"]
dataset_size: 1509 patients total (12 development, 1497 test), 21,605 3D images; external: 20 training, 40 test
limitations: CT scan protocol tailored to left side of heart, low contrast in right side; quantitative evaluation only on subset due to manual workload; 2D analysis only for test set; 4D images analyzed with 3D CNNs, not true 4D.
future_work: Collect 4D CT with cardiac MRI for LVEF comparison; quantify other markers; explore true 4D CNN segmentation.

screening_notes: The paper validates a commercial autocontouring model (RSL RayMachine) for head and neck OAR segmentation across different patient positions. It uses deep learning (3D CNN U-Net) and reports quantitative metrics (DSC, HD95, surface DSC), but it does not propose a new method or architecture. It is a clinical validation study, not a methodological contribution.
exclusion_reason: Only applies existing methods without methodological contribution; validation study of a commercial deep-learning model, no novel architecture or significant improvement presented.
title: Validation of a deep-learning segmentation model for adult and pediatric head and neck radiotherapy in different patient positions

screening_notes: The paper compares deep learning segmentation with deformable and rigid registration for autodelineation in proton therapy. While it uses CT scans and reports Dice/Hausdorff metrics, deep learning is only one of several methods evaluated, and the primary contribution is a workflow feasibility study rather than a novel deep learning method. Therefore, it does not meet criteria 1 and 6 for inclusion.
exclusion_reason: Deep learning is not the primary segmentation method; the paper evaluates multiple autodelineation methods (DLS, DIR, RIR) in a clinical workflow without proposing a novel deep learning architecture or significant methodological contribution.
title: Autodelineation methods in a simulated fully automated proton therapy workflow for esophageal cancer

screening_notes: Paper presents a modified 3D U-Net for kidney parenchyma segmentation in CT, reports Dice coefficient (0.89), uses 3D volumetric processing, and is a novel method. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Measurement of Glomerular Filtration Rate using Quantitative SPECT/CT and Deep-learning-based Kidney Segmentation
architecture_details: Modified 3D U-Net with pre-activation residual blocks, leaky ReLU, 3D spatial dropout (rate 0.3), element-wise sum array, symmetric skip connections
loss_function: Dice similarity coefficient
preprocessing: Resampled CT and SPECT images and manual VOIs to same matrix and voxel sizes (256x256x232, 1.726 mm^3), cropped to 192x128x96, applied 3D volume smoothing and morphological operations to manual VOIs
datasets: ["Retrospective SPECT/CT dataset (393 patients)", "Urolithiasis and kidney donor validation cohort (88 patients)"]
dataset_size: 393 patients for training/validation; 88 patients for clinical validation
limitations: Insufficient data for unusual cases (e.g., small patients, single kidney) leading to segmentation errors; need more training data for single-kidney cases; further clinical validation needed for complicated cases like multi-cystic dysplastic kidneys.
future_work: Further clinical validation of deep-learning-based segmentation is required to expand its use in more complicated cases such as multi-cystic dysplastic kidneys.

screening_notes: The paper demonstrates liver segmentation using a U-Net with VGG-11 backbone on the MSD Liver dataset, but the main novelty is the DP-SGD implementation. The segmentation task is used as a benchmark for the privacy framework, not as the primary contribution. Additionally, the input is 2D slices, not 3D volumes.
exclusion_reason: The paper's primary contribution is a differential privacy framework (deepee), not a novel 3D organ segmentation method. It processes 2D slices (256x256 images) from CT volumes rather than full 3D volumes, failing the 3D/volumetric criterion. The deep learning focus is on privacy-preserving training, not on segmentation architecture development.
title: Medical imaging deep learning with differential privacy

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (DALU-Net), 3D volumetric processing, organ segmentation (liver and lobes), CT modality, quantitative metrics (Dice, IoU, Hausdorff), and novel architecture contribution.
title: Deep 3D attention CLSTM U-Net based automated liver segmentation and volumetry for the liver transplantation in abdominal CT volumes
architecture_details: DALU-Net (Deep Attention LSTM U-Net): combines attention mechanism (AG), deep supervision (DS), and convolutional LSTM (CLSTM) in the decoder; uses 3D convolutions and inter-slice context learning.
loss_function: Dice loss
preprocessing: Window level 50, window width 180; resized to 256x256 in-plane; input shape 64x256x256x1
datasets: ["Gachon University Gil Hospital liver donor CT dataset (in-house)"]
dataset_size: 191 CT scans (from 191 donors)
other_metrics: {"IoU": {"left lobe": 0.787, "right lobe": 0.896, "caudate lobe": 0.936, "whole liver": 0.855}, "Hausdorff distance (mm)": {"left lobe": 6.629, "right lobe": 5.074, "caudate lobe": 1.238, "whole liver": 2.762}, "R^2 for volumetry": {"left lobe": 0.98, "right lobe": 0.996, "caudate lobe": 0.953, "whole liver": 0.996}}
comparison_methods: ["3D U-Net", "Attention U-Net", "Attention U-Net with Deep Supervision"]
limitations: Contrast agent injection amount and scan time vary; section thickness of 5 mm leads to insufficient 3D context; difficulty distinguishing myocardium from liver; need more extensive testing.
future_work: Additional work to improve performance in cases with low accuracy; more extensive testing; additional training data.

screening_notes: The paper presents a hybrid pipeline combining variational methods with a CNN for 3D segmentation of CT scans (aorta, abdominal organs) and MRI (brain tumors). Deep learning is a primary component, 3D volumes are processed, organs are segmented, CT is used, quantitative metrics are reported, and a novel hybrid method is proposed. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Evaluation of a hybrid pipeline for automated segmentation of solid lesions based on mathematical algorithms and deep learning
architecture_details: Hybrid pipeline combining a variational method (edge detection + intensity/location segmentation) with a CNN; CNN receives both the scan and the variational initial segmentation as input. Simplified networks with lighter architectures also tested in appendix.
loss_function: Not specified
preprocessing: Windowing; selection of uppermost and lowermost slice; image registration to superimpose initial segmentation from a reference volume onto new scans.
datasets: ["Aortic CT (post-EVAR, local)", "BraTS (MRI, brain tumors)", "Abdomen (Multi-Atlas Labelling Beyond the Cranial Vault)"]
dataset_size: 70 aortic CTs (50 training, 10 validation, 10 test; 20 unlabeled used in training), 200 BraTS volumes (120 train, 40 val, 40 test), 30 Abdomen CTs (15 train, 5 val, 10 test)
comparison_methods: ["Standard deep learning method (CNN without variational input)", "Variational method only"]
inference_time: 11.6 s for aortic volumes; 2.05 s for abdominal organs; 3.73 s for brain tumors
limitations: Limited testing; accuracy may not be reproducible on other organs, different scan settings, poor boundary conditions, or artifacts. More extensive training/testing needed for generalizability.
future_work: Test and refine pipeline on similar clinical tasks (e.g., preoperative CT scans of aorta); use as baseline for serial comparison; further testing on larger datasets before clinical translation.

screening_notes: Paper presents a novel 3D U-Net variant (DA-UNet) with residual blocks, atrous inception, deep supervision, and CRF post-processing for liver segmentation from CT. Uses 3D convolutions, reports quantitative metrics (Dice, VOE, etc.) on multiple datasets, and is a methodological contribution.
title: Deep supervision and atrous inception-based U-Net combining CRF for automatic liver segmentation from CT
architecture_details: DA-UNet: 3D U-Net with residual blocks in encoder, atrous inception (AI) module connecting encoder and decoder, deep supervision (DS) in decoder, and dense CRF post-processing
loss_function: Tversky loss (α=0.4, β=0.6) with deep supervision auxiliary losses
preprocessing: Downsample to 256×256, locate liver region and expand 20 slices, Hounsfield intensity window [-200,200], set z-spacing to 1mm, normalize to [0,1]
dataset_size: LiTS17: 116 train, 15 test; 3DIRCADb: 10 train, 10 test; SLiver07: 10 train, 10 test
comparison_methods: ["Christ et al. (2D Cascaded FCN)", "Chlebus et al. (2D U-Net)", "Han et al. (2D ResNet)", "Seo et al. (2D mU-Net)", "Li et al. (3D H-DenseUNet)", "3D U-Net (baseline)", "3D ResU-Net", "3D AI-UNet"]
limitations: Large number of 3D network parameters making training difficult and slow; prone to errors when liver boundary contains tumors.
future_work: Simplify network architecture, add bottleneck layer to reduce parameters, and extend to liver tumor segmentation.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (CNN) is primary method, processes 3D CT volumes via multi-projection classification, segments kidney and spleen organs, uses CT modality, reports quantitative metrics (F1, VOE, RVD, ASSD, MSSD), and presents a novel method.
title: Localization of spleen and kidney organs from CT scans based on classification of slices in rotational views
architecture_details: Three separate CNNs (RoiNetX, RoiNetY, RoiNetZ) for X, Y, Z projections; each has 2 conv layers, batch norm, ReLU, max pooling, fully connected, softmax.
loss_function: Cross-entropy (implied by classification layer)
preprocessing: Generation of learning data by extracting slices in X, Y, Z projections; scaling for RoiNetX and RoiNetY; point generation with spacing.
postprocessing: Adaptive fuzzy K-means clustering, morphological operations (dilation, hole filling, largest component selection).
datasets: ["Private CT dataset from Military Institute of Medicine (Warsaw, Poland)"]
dataset_size: 90 CT scans
inference_time: 3.25 s per 512x512 image; ROI generation 2.86 s per case
limitations: Higher implementation complexity; need for three networks; post-processing required; challenges with overlapping organ boundaries.
future_work: Extending to other organs (liver, pancreas); detecting renal/splenic abnormalities.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (3D U-Net + 2D U-Net) as primary method, processes 3D CT volumes, segments multiple heart structures (organs), reports Dice scores, and presents a novel framework combining deep learning with graph matching.
title: Graph matching and deep neural networks based whole heart and great vessel segmentation in congenital heart disease
architecture_details: Combines 3D U-Net for chambers and myocardium segmentation, 2D U-Net for blood pool segmentation, and graph matching for great vessel classification
loss_function: Dice loss + cross-entropy loss
preprocessing: ROI cropping, resizing to 64x64x64, data normalization, data augmentation (same as Ref.8)
postprocessing: Chambers and myocardium refinement using blood pool segmentation; graph matching for vessel classification; region growing for leftover vessels
dataset_size: 68 3D CTA images
limitations: Limited GPU memory limits 3D U-net to down-sampled CT, boundary extraction errors in blood pool segmentation, threshold-based ground truth limits differentiation, lack of clinical-level criterion for training
future_work: Use more advanced GPUs to process larger dimensions, fusion/ensemble network, two-stage training strategy

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (UNETR), 3D CT volumes, organ segmentation (liver), quantitative metrics (DSC, MSD, HD95), and novel contribution (fully automatic right lobe graft weight estimation).
title: Estimation of right lobe graft weight for living donor liver transplantation using deep learning-based fully automatic computed tomographic volumetry
architecture_details: UNETR with transformer encoder (12 layers, embedding size 768, patch resolution 16x16x16) and CNN decoder; two-step pipeline: (1) whole liver segmentation, (2) right/left lobe classification
loss_function: Not specified
preprocessing: Resampled to isotropic 1.0 mm voxel spacing; random cropping to 32x32x32 volumes; data augmentation with random flips in axial, sagittal, coronal views
postprocessing: 3D connected component method; morphological erosion (radius 1, 3 times) and dilation (radius 1, 3 times)
dataset_size: 248 CT scans (188 training, 40 validation, 20 test)
comparison_methods: ["Kwon et al. (2020) manual CT volumetry", "Existing deep learning methods on Synapse dataset (TransUNet, Swin-Unet, Swin UNETR)"]
limitations: Single-center study; only delayed phase CT; excluded patients with liver masses/cirrhosis; linear volume-to-weight formula may cause underestimation
future_work: Collect multi-center data; extend to other CT phases; develop non-linear volume-to-weight conversion formula

screening_notes: Paper applies 3D nnU-Net to renal parenchyma and cortex segmentation for CKD evaluation. Meets criteria 1-5 (deep learning, 3D, organ segmentation, CT, quantitative metrics) but fails criterion 6 (novel contribution) and matches exclusion criterion 7.
exclusion_reason: Only applies existing methods without methodological contribution (uses 3D nnU-Net as-is, no novel architecture or significant improvement)
title: AI-based segmentation of renal enhanced CT images for quantitative evaluate of chronic kidney disease

screening_notes: Paper proposes a novel knowledge distillation method (GTAN) for 3D liver CT segmentation using 3D U-Net. It processes 3D CT volumes, segments liver (organ), uses CT modality, reports quantitative metrics (Dice, IoU, HD95), and presents a new architecture/improvement. No exclusion criteria apply.
title: Efficient knowledge distillation for liver CT segmentation using growing assistant network
architecture_details: U-Net with varying sizes (filters and depths) for teacher, student, and teacher assistants; also V-Net used as teacher. Proposed GTAN (growing teacher assistant network) for knowledge distillation.
loss_function: Combination of KD loss (KL divergence) and segmentation loss (optimized IoU loss)
preprocessing: Intensity truncation (35 HU ± 400 HU), 3D resampling to 2.5 mm resolution, use of three contrast phases (arterial, portal, delayed) as natural augmentation

screening_notes: The paper uses a 3D U-Net for lung cancer tumor (GTV) segmentation, not organ segmentation. It focuses on uncertainty maps and clinical validation, but the target is tumor, not organs. Therefore excluded.

screening_notes: Paper proposes a novel data augmentation strategy using statistical shape model and 3D thin plate spline, applied to deep learning segmentation. screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning primary, 3D volumetric processing, organ segmentation (heart substructures), CT modality, quantitative metrics (Dice, Jaccard), novel contribution (three attention mechanisms).
title: Improving Whole-Heart CT Image Segmentation by Attention Mechanism

screening_notes: Paper uses CNN and stacked denoising autoencoders for heart segmentation from CT images, but processes each slice independently; no 3D convolutions or volumetric processing. The paper also includes PET image segmentation via saliency, but the primary deep learning method is 2D.

screening_notes: The paper proposes a 2D U-Net variant with channel attention and cross-level feature fusion for segmenting esophagus and esophageal cancer from CT slices. Although a 3D semi-automatic segmentation method is described, it is not a deep learning 3D model; it simply propagates 2D segmentations across slices. Thus, it fails the 3D/volumetric criterion.
exclusion_reason: Does not process 3D CT volumes with deep learning; processes 2D slices independently. The deep learning model is 2D U-Net, and 3D reconstruction is a post-processing step, not a 3D volumetric deep learning approach.
title: Channel-Attention U-Net: Channel Attention Mechanism for Semantic Segmentation of Esophagus and Esophageal Cancer
architecture: U-Net with Channel Attention Module (CAM) and Cross-level Feature Fusion Module (CFFM)
architecture_details: Based on U-Net, adds CAM and CFFM. 2D convolutions, 3x3 kernels, encoder-decoder with skip connections.
loss_function: Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE)
preprocessing: Convert DICOM to 512x512 bitmap, crop 80x80 region containing esophagus, data augmentation (cropping, translation) to increase 5x
postprocessing: 3D semi-automatic segmentation method to propagate segmentation across slices, then 3D rendering
datasets: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center chest CT scans
dataset_size: 152 patients, 13,050 CT images manually labeled; training set 46,400 samples (after augmentation), validation 11,600, test 7,250
limitations: Segmentation effect on some small boundaries is not good enough; if there is a very small gap between other similar tissues and the esophagus, sometimes parts of similar tissues are seen as prediction regions; if there is a small boundary in the esophagus with air hole that is blocked by other tissues, the network will ignore that portion.
future_work: Improve edge enhancement capabilities of the network to solve this problem.

screening_notes: Paper proposes Eso-Net, a novel 2.5D segmentation network for cancerous esophagus in CT. Uses deep learning (U-Net based) with 3D structural priors (MSRF) and channel-wise 2.5D processing (adjacent slices), thus qualifies as 3D/volumetric. Segments an organ (esophagus), uses CT, reports quantitative metrics (Dice, precision, sensitivity, Hausdorff), and presents novel architecture. Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Eso-Net: A Novel 2.5D Segmentation Network With the Multi-Structure Response Filter for the Cancerous Esophagus
architecture_details: 2.5D segmentation network with channel-wise concatenation of three adjacent slices, dilated convolutions and residual connections in encoder/decoder blocks, Prior Attention Modules (PAM) in skip connections, and Multi-Structure Response Filter (MSRF) for 3D structural priors.
loss_function: Dice loss
preprocessing: Window level (WL) and window width (WW) set to 40 and 200; intensity values between -160 and 240 linearly normalized to [0,1]; Multi-Structure Response Filter (MSRF) applied to enhance surrounding tissues; cropping 144x144 ROI from center; channel-wise concatenation of three adjacent slices.
dataset_size: 30 esophageal cancer patients, 6362 CT slices
limitations: Generalization capacity limited by small dataset size; MSRF is untrainable and requires manual parameter tuning for other tasks.
future_work: Optimizing architecture on larger dataset and merging MSRF with deep learning model.

screening_notes: Paper proposes a novel 3D DenseNet with 3D-ASPP module for volumetric CT organ segmentation. Uses 3D convolutions, segments multiple thoracic organs, reports quantitative metrics (Dice, Jaccard, etc.), and presents a new architecture. Meets all inclusion criteria.

architecture_details: Hybrid network combining 3D DenseNet (encoder-decoder) with a 3D-Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module. Dense blocks with PReLU activation and batch normalization. 3D convolutions with kernel size 3x3x3.

comparison_methods: ["3D simple-VNet", "3D attention U-Net", "Dense V-Net", "2D T-Net", "3D U-Net", "V-Net", "cascaded 3D U-Net", "ensemble methods"]
limitations: Computational complexity increases with large feature maps; limited GPU memory; small organs may be challenging to segment; overfitting risk with limited data.
future_work: Explore new models based on attention mechanism or incorporate different parameters to generalize and train well for another medical dataset.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (U-Net/V-Net), 3D volumetric processing, multi-organ segmentation, CT modality, quantitative metrics (Dice, Jaccard, sensitivity), and novel contribution (FBP-derived domain adaptation).

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (FRV-Net), 3D volumetric processing, organ segmentation (lung lobes), CT modality, quantitative metrics (Dice), and novel contribution (regularized V-Net). No exclusion criteria apply.

venue: 2018 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)

organs_segmented: ["Lung lobes (5 lobes: right upper, right middle, right lower, left upper, left lower)"]

title: AbdomenAtlasNet-3.0: Multi-Phase Deep Learning for Robust Multi-Organ Segmentation of Core Abdominal Structures on a Large-Scale CT Atlas
architecture_details: Separate encoders for each CT phase (non-contrast, arterial, portal-venous), channel-wise squeeze-and-excitation attention at each resolution level, shared decoder, modality-presence masks for missing phases.
loss_function: Composite loss: soft Dice loss + weighted cross-entropy loss (λ=0.7 for Dice, class weights inverse frequency)
preprocessing: Resampled to 1.5×1.5×1.5 mm³, cropped to body bounding box, intensity clipped to [-200,300] HU, normalized to [0,1], rigid registration of secondary phases to portal-venous, patch sampling (160×160×160) with 50% organ-centered, 50% uniform.
dataset_size: 3,220 CT volumes (2,254 train, 322 val, 644 test)
training_time: Not specified (300 epochs with early stopping)
limitations: Primary endpoint is geometric segmentation accuracy, not clinical outcomes; restricted to CT and nine organs; no external prospective validation; not compared to transformer-based architectures.
future_work: Extend to joint organ-and-tumor segmentation, integrate with non-CT modalities, cross-modality transfer learning, compare with transformer-based multimodal architectures.

screening_notes: Paper presents Onco-Seg, a deep learning adaptation of SAM3 for multi-modal medical segmentation including CT. It processes 3D volumes via slice tracking, segments organs (liver, pancreas, etc.), reports quantitative metrics (Dice, IoU), and introduces novel contributions (LoRA fine-tuning, modality-specific preprocessing, DDP fixes). Meets all inclusion criteria.
title: Onco-Seg: Adapting Promptable Concept Segmentation for Multi-Modal Medical Imaging
architecture: SAM3 (Segment Anything Model 3) with LoRA adaptation
architecture_details: Adaptation of SAM3 with LoRA on attention layers (qkv, proj), frozen perception encoder (800M params), DDP device placement fix, grounding stability injection, modality-specific preprocessing.
loss_function: Combined Dice-Focal loss with modality-specific weighting (λ_dice, λ_focal, γ)
preprocessing: Modality-specific normalization: CT windowing [-1000,1000], MRI percentile clipping, ultrasound percentile, etc. Also foreground-biased slice sampling (80% foreground), channel selection for multi-channel MRI (e.g., BraTS 4→3 channels).
dataset_size: Training: 98,154 cases across 35 datasets; Evaluation: 12 datasets (sizes not fully specified)
training_time: Not specified (epochs vary by dataset size; e.g., 30 epochs for BraTS and MSD Liver)
limitations: Performance degrades for lesions <10mm diameter; PET imaging requires dedicated training; Multi-class segmentation (BTCV) remains challenging.
future_work: Short-Term: Integrate uncertainty quantification; develop 3D Slicer plugin. Medium-Term: Multi-center clinical validation; federated learning. Long-Term: Foundation model for all medical segmentation; FDA 510(k) regulatory pathway.

screening_notes: Paper presents a deployment framework for deep learning segmentation models, not a novel segmentation method. It is classified as a framework per study type routing. The framework supports CT and MR, includes organ segmentation, and is relevant to the systematic review. No quantitative metrics are reported, but framework papers use the qualitative template only.
title: Portable framework to deploy deep learning segmentation models for medical images
components: CERR platform extension; pre/post-processing configurations via JSON; packaging with Singularity containers (Linux) and Conda environment archives (Windows, macOS, Linux); supports DICOM and planC input/output; visualization, radiomics, dosimetric analysis; integration with clinical software like MIM via extensions; supports MATLAB, Octave, Python; includes preprocessing operations (resampling, cropping, resizing, orientation, modality, filters, channel population) and postprocessing (connected components, label maps).
license: Open-source, GNU GPL (GNU-copyrighted) with CERR platform; model developers retain copyright to their models.
benchmark_reproduction: No quantitative benchmark results reported; framework used to deploy five in-house models across H&N, Lung, Prostate, and Brain sites, and used in clinical workflow and for segmenting large public datasets for outcomes studies.

screening_notes: The paper is a community-driven overview of AI deployment challenges and solutions, with case studies. It mentions MONAI Deploy but does not present a novel method or quantitative evaluation for organ segmentation.
exclusion_reason: This is a viewpoint/review paper discussing AI deployment in radiology, not a novel deep learning method for 3D organ segmentation. It does not present a new architecture, quantitative segmentation metrics, or focus on CT organ segmentation. It fails inclusion criteria 1, 5, and 6.

screening_notes: Confirmed as a software framework for AI-assisted interactive labeling of 3D medical images, including deep learning-based segmentation. It supports 3D CT volumes and organ segmentation, and reports quantitative metrics (Dice) in its evaluation. The paper is a framework contribution, not a novel segmentation method, so it is routed to the qualitative template.
components: Client-server architecture with GUI integrations (3D Slicer, OHIF), interactive segmentation models (DeepGrow, DeepEdit, Scribbles-based), non-interactive automatic segmentation, active learning strategies (dropout-based uncertainty, TTA), heuristic planner for GPU optimization, DICOMWeb support, and REST API for custom app development.
benchmark_reproduction: Evaluated on Spleen MSD dataset (41 CT volumes) with DeepGrow: validation Dice improved from 0.891 (stage 1) to 0.967 (2D) and 0.959 (3D) at stage 4, with annotation time reduced to 1-2.5 minutes per volume. DeepEdit on cardiac CMR (left atrium) showed progressive Dice improvement with continuous annotation and training, reducing total annotation time compared to manual methods.

screening_notes: This paper introduces MONAI, an open-source PyTorch-based framework for deep learning in healthcare, with a focus on medical imaging. It provides domain-specific transforms, network architectures, loss functions, and workflows for 3D medical image segmentation. Although it does not report quantitative organ segmentation metrics, it is a software framework/tool for 3D medical image segmentation and is therefore included as a framework study.
components: MONAI Core modules: monai.data (datasets, readers/writers), monai.losses (loss functions), monai.networks (network definitions), monai.transforms (pre/post-processing), monai.csrc and monai.extensions (C++/CUDA extensions), monai.visualize (visualization utilities), monai.metrics (metric tracking), monai.optimizers (optimizers), monai.engines and monai.handlers (workflow engines and event handlers). Also includes MONAI Label (annotation), MONAI Deploy (deployment), MONAI FL (federated learning), and MONAI Education.
benchmark_reproduction: Provides tools for benchmarking and performance optimization, including support for MedNIST and Medical Segmentation Decathlon datasets. No specific quantitative benchmark results are reported in the paper.
release_version: No specific version number mentioned; paper describes MONAI Core as of 2022.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning primary, 3D CT organ segmentation, quantitative metrics (Dice, NSD), novel architecture (U-Mamba).
title: U-Mamba: Enhancing Long-range Dependency for Biomedical Image Segmentation
architecture_details: Hybrid CNN-SSM block combining Residual blocks and Mamba (SSM) blocks; encoder-decoder with U-Mamba blocks in encoder, Residual blocks in decoder; self-configuring like nnU-Net; two variants: U-Mamba_Bot (bottleneck only) and U-Mamba_Enc (all encoder blocks)
loss_function: unweighted sum of Dice loss and cross-entropy
preprocessing: Default image preprocessing in nnU-Net
datasets: ["FLARE 2022 Abdomen CT (training from MSD Pancreas and AbdomenCT-1K)", "AMOS 2022 Abdomen MRI", "EndoVis 2017", "Cell Segmentation Challenge"]
dataset_size: 50 training CT scans (4794 slices) and 50 testing CT scans (10894 slices)
organs_segmented: ["liver", "spleen", "pancreas", "right kidney", "left kidney", "stomach", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "right adrenal gland", "left adrenal gland", "duodenum"]
limitations: Limited training data (50 CT scans); Transformer baselines may be under-optimized due to single GPU training; complementary performance with nnU-Net suggests potential for ensemble.
future_work: Leverage large-scale datasets for training U-Mamba to create deployable segmentation tools or pre-trained weights; integrate with advanced techniques like strong data augmentation, loss functions for imbalanced targets, region-based training; apply U-Mamba block to classification and detection networks.

screening_notes: Meets all inclusion criteria: deep learning (SegResNet), 3D CT volumes, organ segmentation (127 classes), quantitative metrics (Dice), novel contribution (unified automatic+interactive foundation model). Confirmed as a software framework/tool for 3D medical image segmentation (VISTA3D).
components: Automatic branch (promptable class embedding) and interactive branch (3D point clicks) sharing a SegResNet encoder, with a merger algorithm for refinement; supervoxel generation from SAM features; four-stage training recipe.
license: Not explicitly stated; code and weights publicly available on GitHub (https://github.com/Project-MONAI/VISTA).
benchmark_reproduction: Benchmarked on 14 datasets with 127 classes, comparing with Auto3DSeg, nnU-Net, TotalSegmentator, MedSAM, SegVol; reported Dice scores and inference times.
release_version: Not specified; code and weights available at https://github.com/Project-MONAI/VISTA

screening_notes: The paper presents nnInteractive, a 3D interactive segmentation framework built on nnU-Net. It uses deep learning (UNet-based), processes 3D volumes, supports organ segmentation across multiple modalities including CT, reports quantitative Dice metrics, and introduces novel prompting mechanisms (lasso, scribbles, etc.) and AutoZoom. It is explicitly integrated into Napari and MITK, making it a software framework/tool for 3D medical image segmentation. Therefore, it meets all inclusion criteria and is classified as a framework.
components: UNet-based architecture (ResEnc-L from nnU-Net) with early prompting; supports points, scribbles, bounding boxes, and lasso prompts; AutoZoom mechanism for large structures; interaction simulation agents (Random, Sunk Cost, Single Interaction); SuperVoxels for label diversity; integration with Napari and MITK Workbench; Python backend.
license: Not explicitly stated in the paper; publicly available but license unspecified.
benchmark_reproduction: Benchmarked on RadioActive benchmark, expert scribble benchmark (MS-CMRSeg 2019), and a radiological user study. Outperforms SAM, SAM2, MedSAM, ScribblePrompt, SegVol, SAM-Med3D, and others. For point prompts, achieves 10.1 Dice points over ScribblePrompt; for boxes, 14.9 over SAM2; for scribbles, 23.8 over ScribblePrompt. Interactive refinement reaches >70 Dice across datasets. Expert scribble benchmark: nnInteractive achieves 87.29 average Dice with all slices, 84.29 with only 3 slices, vs ScribblePrompt 80.98.
release_version: No specific version number mentioned; publicly available as Napari plugin, MITK integration, and Python backend.
